chunks: And from him (Al-Hassan ibn Ali) from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about making up the night prayer, so he said: 'Make it up in the time in which you prayed it.' I said: 'Will there be two Witr prayers in one night?' He said: 'It is not two Witr prayers in one night, one of them is for what was missed by you.'

key_terms.قَضَاءُ: making up a missed obligatory act
key_terms.لِمَا فَاتَكَ: for what was missed by you

ai.seo_question: How should the missed night prayer be made up according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS), the concept of Qada (making up) for Salat al-Layl is clarified to ensure that performing the makeup prayer does not result in two distinct Witr prayers. The Imam explains that the makeup prayer serves as the completion of the missed obligation, maintaining the singular nature of the night prayer's concluding segment. This ruling highlights the precision in Shia jurisprudence regarding the timing and classification of voluntary yet emphasized prayers.
